item.title: The Versatile Blogger Award Nomination
item.description: It’s not every day that one gets to find nice surprises in their inbox, but today was one of those days for me! 😀 The one who made the surprise is Veronika from Departure and Arrivals (departurearrivals.com, no longer online), who nominated me for the The Versatile Blogger Award! It was the first time I’ve heard about the award, but it seems like a great way for bloggers to show their appreciation to other amazing bloggers whose stories they enjoy! Thank you Veronika for nominating me, I’m so glad my blog is inspiring 🙂 This is the perfect incentive I need in order to improve my blog and my writing!

item.title: Cool untranslatable foreign words
item.description: hygge - weirdly pronounced Danish word that seems to mean cosiness and can be applied to almost anything apparently. There’s a pretty good explanation on visitdenmark.com (visitdenmark.com/danish-meaning-hygge, no longer online) and I’ve also found a list of 9 ways to get more hygge 🙂

item.title: 10 things I learned while roadtripping to Mont Blanc
item.description:
“Travel is the best teacher.”

Together with some friends, I recently took a roadtrip to Mont Blanc. We climbed the highest peak in western Europe and then returned home through Venice 🙂 Here are the most important life lessons I’ve learned from this trip:

item.title: How does the temperature vary in the atmosphere?
item.description: I usually like travelling by plane … that is when I manage not to think about all the things that could go wrong 😛 Luckily I’ve recently read a really cool book on air travel, Cockpit confidential by Patrick Smith, which has helped reduce some of my worries. Apart from the images from TV with planes that break in half and people flying around, there are also lots of questions that pop into my head while high up in the clouds. Like how does the temperature vary in the atmosphere? This question popped into my head when I was watching on the screen that map that shows the route and a tiny plane that slooowly moves closer to the destination. The screen also showed the outside temperature of -50 degrees Celsius. After landing safely, instead of properly enjoying my holiday, I looked for a bit online and found an image with the way the temperature of the atmosphere varies depending on height.
